did_you_know.text: Did you know? The Philistines and Israel camped on opposite sides of the Valley of Elah: the Philistines between Socoh and Azekah, and Israel in the valley itself, with the ravine separating the two armies.
Did you know? Goliath is described as a champion who came out from between the camps and offered to settle the matter through single combat. He is described as being six cubits and a span tall.
Did you know? Goliath was heavily armed: he wore scale armor weighing five thousand bronze shekels, and he wore a bronze helmet and bronze greaves on his legs.
Did you know? Goliath’s spear shaft was like a weaver’s beam, and the spearhead weighed six hundred iron shekels. A shield bearer walked in front of him.
Did you know? Goliath did not issue his challenge only once: for forty days, he came forward every morning and evening and stood before the Israelite army.

Did you know? Jesse sent David to his brothers with food: an ephah of roasted grain, ten loaves of bread, and ten cheeses. He also asked David to see how they were doing and bring back a pledge from them.
Did you know? David saw Goliath’s challenge as not only a military threat but also a disgrace against the army of Israel and the living God.

Did you know? David explained his willingness to fight by saying that he had already rescued sheep from a lion and a bear. He regarded Goliath as an enemy who should be struck down because he had defied the armies of the living God.
Did you know? David did not use Saul’s armor and weapons because he was not accustomed to them. Instead, he took his staff, chose five smooth stones from the stream, and held his sling in his hand.

Did you know? David emphasized that victory does not depend on sword or spear, but on the LORD: “For the battle is the LORD’s.” He then struck Goliath with a stone, used Goliath’s sword, and the Philistines fled.
